recipes.title: Italian baked potato croquettes, light
recipes.summary: Golden baked potato croquettes with spinach, basil and parmesan. Extra greens and less cheese, bread and oil keep this Italian snack lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the potato, spinach, onion, garlic, bread and basil in their listed forms.
Pulse the bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Cook the onion in half the olive oil until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the garlic into the onion until fragrant.
Fold the spinach into the pan until wilted and fairly dry.
Mash the potato until smooth.
Mix the potato, eggs, parmesan cheese, spinach mixture, basil and salt until evenly combined.
Shape the potato mixture into small croquettes.
Roll each croquette in the bread crumbs.
Brush the croquettes with the remaining olive oil.
Bake the croquettes until crisp and golden all over.
Rest the Italian baked potato croquettes before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven until crisp. Freeze baked croquettes for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Japanese tamagoyaki breakfast plate, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Japanese breakfast plate with tender rolled omelette, steamed rice, mushrooms, spinach and cool cucumber.

steps.instruction: Cook the white rice until tender and fully steamed.
Prepare the mushrooms, spinach, cucumber and spring onions in their listed forms.
Whisk the eggs, vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and salt until evenly combined.
Heat half the sesame oil in a non-stick frying pan.
Cook the mushrooms until tender and lightly browned.
Fold the spinach into the mushrooms until wilted.
Transfer the mushrooms and spinach to a plate.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in the clean frying pan.
Pour a thin layer of the egg mixture into the pan.
Roll the softly set egg layer into a tight log.
Repeat with the remaining egg mixture until a thick tamagoyaki forms.
Rest the tamagoyaki so the layers firm slightly.
Slice the tamagoyaki into even pieces.
Arrange the white rice, mushrooms, spinach and cucumber on serving plates.
Finish the Japanese tamagoyaki breakfast plate with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served fresh. Refrigerate the tamagoyaki, rice and vegetables separately for up to 2 days. Reheat the rice and omelette gently. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Thai shrimp rice noodle salad, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Thai lunch of rice noodles, seared shrimp and crisp vegetables tossed with a bright fish-sauce, lime, garlic and ginger dressing.

steps.instruction: Prepare the shrimp, cucumber, carrot, green cabbage, bean sprouts, spring onions, cilantro, garlic, lime and ginger in their listed forms.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic and ginger into a dressing.
Cook the rice noodles until tender but still springy.
Rinse the rice noodles under cold water and drain them thoroughly.
Coat the shrimp with one third of the dressing.
Rest the shrimp so it absorbs the seasoning.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan.
Cook the shrimp until pink, opaque and lightly browned.
Cool the shrimp until just warm.
Combine the rice noodles, cucumber, carrot, green cabbage and bean sprouts.
Add the shrimp, spring onions and cilantro to the noodle salad.
Toss the Thai shrimp rice noodle salad with the remaining dressing.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled shortly before serving. Refrigerate the shrimp, noodles, vegetables and dressing separately for up to 2 days. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Chinese tomato and egg noodles, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Chinese noodle dinner with soft scrambled eggs, spinach and a bright savoury tomato sauce scented with sesame and spring onions.

steps.instruction: Prepare the onion, spinach, spring onions and garlic in their listed forms.
Cook the rice noodles until tender but still springy.
Rinse the rice noodles briefly and drain them thoroughly.
Beat the eggs with half the salt until evenly combined.
Heat half the sesame oil in a wide frying pan.
Scramble the eggs until softly set.
Transfer the eggs to a clean plate.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in the pan.
Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the garlic into the onion until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, brown sugar, vegetable broth and remaining salt.
Simmer the tomato sauce until thick and glossy.
Fold the spinach into the tomato sauce until wilted.
Return the eggs and add the soy sauce.
Toss the rice noodles through the tomato and egg sauce.
Finish the Chinese tomato and egg noodles with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat quickly in a hot pan with a splash of vegetable broth. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: French creamy mushroom tartines, light
recipes.summary: Crisp tartines topped with mushrooms and leeks in a light thyme cream sauce, finished with a little parmesan and baked until golden.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the bread, mushrooms, leek, onion, garlic and parmesan cheese in their listed forms.
Toast the bread in the oven until dry and lightly crisp.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan.
Cook the onion and leek until soft and lightly golden.
Cook the mushrooms until their moisture evaporates and the edges brown.
Stir the garlic and thyme into the mushrooms until fragrant.
Pour the heavy cream and whole milk into the pan.
Simmer the mushroom sauce until it thickens enough to mound on bread.
Stir half the parmesan cheese and the salt into the sauce.
Spoon the creamy mushroom mixture over the toasted bread.
Scatter the remaining parmesan cheese over the tartines.
Bake the French creamy mushroom tartines until bubbling and golden.
Rest the tartines briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten warm. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven until the bread is crisp. Freezing is not recommended.
